articles.t: GTA 6 aurait pu aller encore plus loin : Rockstar révèle ses idées abandonnées
Sans disque dans la boîte, GTA 6 réussit le plus gros lancement physique britannique depuis 2019 — Frandroid
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 a rapporté 32 millions de livres sterling, environ 38 millions d'euros, en trois jours dans les boutiques britanniques. Aucun jeu n'avait fait un aussi bon démarrage physique au Royaume-Uni depuis FIFA 20 en septembre 2019, et la boîte de GTA 6 ne contient pourtant aucun disque, seulement un code de téléchargement.
articles.txt:
Avec GTA 6, Rockstar a fait un choix qui pouvait inquiéter les magasins : la boîte vendue en rayon ne contient qu’un code de téléchargement, sans aucun disque. Ça n’a pas freiné les acheteurs.
D’après les relevés du cabinet Nielsen IQ, publiés ce jeudi 26 novembre par la newsletter spécialisée The Game Business , GTA 6 a fait au Royaume-Uni le plus gros lancement physique depuis 2019. Sorti le 19 novembre 2026 sur PS5 et Xbox Series, le jeu accumulait déjà les records , jusqu’à devenir le plus gros lancement de l’histoire PlayStation .
En trois jours, le jeu a généré 32 millions de livres de revenus outre-Manche. Pour trouver un jeu qui s’était autant vendu en boîte pendant sa première semaine au Royaume-Uni, il faut remonter à FIFA 20, en septembre 2019, avant le Covid.
Dans l’historique des classements britanniques, qui remonte à 1995, GTA 6 arrive au 17e rang des plus gros lancements physiques. Le démarrage serait encore plus fort en France, où plus d’un million de boîtes auraient été vendues en trois jours, selon les informations de The Game Business, soit un volume proche de celui de GTA 5 en 2013. En Espagne, GTA 6 a même signé le plus gros lancement physique de l’histoire du classement national.
GTA 6 ne tourne pas sur PS4. Autrement dit, ceux qui jouaient encore sur l’ancienne génération ont dû changer de console . Au Royaume-Uni, les ventes de PS5 ont bondi de 46 % la semaine du lancement, et celles des Xbox Series S et X ont progressé de 75 %, leur plus forte hausse depuis 2024. Toutes marques confondues, les ventes de consoles ont augmenté de 38 % sur la semaine, après une hausse de 29 % la semaine précédente.
Aux États-Unis, le cabinet d’études Circana a vu l’effet arriver avant même la sortie du jeu. Pendant la semaine qui s’est terminée le 14 novembre, les ventes de PS5 ont été multipliées par 2,4 par rapport à la semaine d’avant, et celles des Xbox Series par 2,3.
Les smartphones aussi ont profité de l’engouement, puisque les anciens GTA ont vu leurs téléchargements sur mobile grimper la même semaine .
Ces classements ne comptent en effet que les boîtes. Or, le 20 novembre, Take-Two, la maison mère de Rockstar, a estimé que GTA 6 avait généré 3,79 milliards de dollars de ventes dans le monde dès son premier jour (environ 3,5 milliards d’euros).
L’éditeur n’a pas indiqué combien de ces ventes venaient des boîtes et combien d’achats en numérique.

articles.txt:
(Image credit: Rockstar Games) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Bluesky Threads Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Grand Theft Auto 6 developer Rockstar Games has an outdated habit of double-dipping on its customers. First comes a console version , and months later, a PC version arrives . By then, a lot of PC gamers have already bought the game once on console, and they're coerced into buying it again.
I think I bought GTA 5 three times over the years as I moved onto different hardware. This time around, GTA 6 has barely been out for a week on Xbox Series X|S and PS5/Pro , and we already have what appears to be a working version of the game on PC .
Hobbyist developers and AI vibe coders have taken it upon themselves to get unofficial GTA 6 builds pulled from consoles running on Windows PC . You might have already seen it proclaimed on social media that GTA 6 has arrived for PC. That's not quite true. Here's what's actually going on, and what it means (and doesn't mean) for PC gamers.
Shortly after the official GTA 6 console launch on November 19 , hacker Cyberleek — the group behind the bulk of the pre-launch gameplay and content leaks — released some significant portions of the Xbox build.
It wasn't until a couple of days later, when the game's executable file was published, that recompilation efforts for Windows PC really kicked off. Within hours of the executable's release, I saw developers posting proof that the game was launching on PC. A few hours later, they were able to get through the game's initial setup.
Since then, and over the past couple of days, recompilation efforts have really ramped up. Today, at the time of writing, someone has posted a clip on Reddit of GTA 6 running on PC at 60+ FPS .
Recent updates The Reddit thread I linked, containing the video of GTA 6 running on PC at 60+ FPS, has already been deleted . You'll have to trust me on this one.
That's some incredible progress in a project that barely launched just a couple of days ago. However, it's still a very long way from becoming a finished, stable port that you or I might want to play through.
Running a console version of a game on PC usually requires emulation . An emulator is essentially a live interpreter, allowing your PC to pretend it's a console while it translates instructions.
This extra layer of work usually saps performance in a major way, especially in a game as demanding and complex as GTA 6. With the rise of powerful, personal AI assistants, recompilation has become the new and preferred way for this type of work.
Imagine you're reading a book written in a language you don't understand. Would you rather have a live interpreter telling you what each line means, or would you rather just read the translated version without all the hassle?
Recompilation works the same way, converting the game's code from console-compatible to natively PC-compatible. If it's done properly, the results can be quite astounding. Just look at the Ocarina of Time remake's unofficial PC port that arrived shortly after the game's real launch on Switch 2.
Recompiling a game's code has always been possible , but it was a matter of time and effort that stopped most projects from going live. Now, with the impressive advances in AI coding tools , console-to-PC conversions have become something that practically anyone with enough token budget can take on.
And that's basically what's going on today, with groups of would-be coders assembling their AI agents into swarms to tackle the massive recompilation task.
The entire GTA 6 recompilation fiasco would probably be getting a lot more attention if it weren't totally illegal because of how the game's files are being leaked and distributed. Rockstar's parent company, Take-Two , has been busy shutting down projects like Leonida , one of the leading efforts to recompile GTA 6 on PC.

articles.t: Pourquoi il n'y a aucune vraie marque dans GTA 6
articles.chapeau: Les marques refusaient de s’afficher dans le premier GTA et les institutions menaçaient d’interdire le jeu. Trente ans plus tard, le rapport de force c’est inversé.
articles.txt:
Les marques refusaient de s’afficher dans le premier GTA et les institutions menaçaient d’interdire le jeu. Trente ans plus tard, le rapport de force c’est inversé.
1997, un jeu vidéo obscur risque la faillite et l'interdiction quand un lord britannique s'empare du sujet et s'emballe à la Chambre haute : « Le gouvernement compte-t-il prendre des mesures concernant la sortie annoncée, plus tard dans l'année, d'un nouveau jeu vidéo intitulé Grand Theft Auto ? » Il dénonce la violence du gameplay qui valorise les crimes et les délits et moque les forces de l’ordre. Ignore-t-il que son indignation a été savamment orchestrée par un expert des coups tordus et des tabloïds anglais ? En suscitant une intense panique morale, Lord Campbell of Croy aura surtout permis à la licence d'exister. Mais si le scandale donne un coup de projecteur, il ne construit pas un modèle économique. l'équipe derrière le jeu est au bord du gouffre financier : l'éditeur est cédé « pour un penny », le studio pour une livre symbolique. Et quand la publicité commence à investir le secteur du jeu vidéo, aucune marque ne veut compromettre son image dans les eaux troubles de GTA. Privé d'annonceurs et en guerre avec les institutions, le titre va faire de cette mise à l'écart sa signature. Il assumera d’être antisystème et irrévérencieux. Trente ans plus tard, le rapport de force s'est inversé. GTA malmène le statut des marques comme celui des institutions réelles pour imposer les règles business de son univers numérique.
« Tout le monde le sait, si vous poussez trop fort avec les partenariats, c'est un désastre. » Début mai 2026, à la conférence iicon de Las Vegas, Strauss Zelnick, le sémillant patron de la maison mère de Rockstar, avait prévenu. Aucune marque réelle ne serait acceptée dans GTA. Pas plus dans le VI que dans les précédents opus. « Je crois que ça nous garde purs », avait-il tranché. Une coquetterie que peu d'univers numériques peuvent se permettre mais sur laquelle GTA a bâti son empire.
Faute d'annonceurs prêts à tremper leur image dans ses eaux troubles, GTA les a tout simplement réinventés. Du fast-food débitant du poulet frit à la chaîne d'information enchaînant les breaking news, de la voiture à gros pot d'échappement au réseau social abrutissant, de la supérette miteuse aux boutiques de luxe clinquantes… Rockstar a non seulement recréé un univers marchand complet, mais la plupart de ses marques détournent et caricaturent les marques réelles. Nike, la déesse de la victoire, devient Eris, celle de la discorde, Fox News, la chaîne du renard malin, cède la place à Weazel News, celle de la belette trompeuse, et Facebook se transforme en Lifeinvader, l'envahisseur de vies. Sur les panneaux de Vice City, la bière Pißwasser, dont le nom signifie « eau de pisse » en allemand, proclame « Vous êtes au pays de la Pißwasser ! ». Pfister, le double de Porsche, invite à rouler « topless » au volant de son cabriolet. Quant à eCola, le Coca-Cola de Vice City, dont le nom évoque E. coli, la bactérie intestinale, elle se dit « délicieusement contagieuse ». Une centaine de marques créées fonctionnent sur ce registre. Elles ont la couleur des marques du monde réel mais l'ironie cinglante des mèmes. Dan Houser, cofondateur de Rockstar et longtemps auteur de la série, a résumé le projet par cette formule : le monde de GTA montre l'Amérique « telle qu'on la voit seulement à travers les films et la publicité ».
Si les marques ont fait de mauvaise publicité bon cœur, les villes ont suivi. Chaque épisode de GTA caricature une métropole américaine, New York en Liberty City, Los Angeles en Los Santos, Miami en Vice City, et celles-ci ont fini, comme les marques, par accepter leur portrait le plus grinçant. Le 10 septembre 2026, quelques semaines avant le lancement de GTA VI, la commission municipale de Miami Beach a discuté âprement les conditions d'apparition du nouvel opus du jeu dans sa ville, qui lui sert de toile de fond. Comme trente ans avant eux le lord britannique, plusieurs élus refusent d'associer la cité à l'univers violent du jeu. Mais la commissaire Tanya Katzoff Bhatt l'emporte avec un argument imparable : le jeu viendra à Miami Beach « avec ou sans nous ».
La scène a un air de déjà-vu. En 1984, la série Miami Vice avait plongé les responsables du tourisme dans une quasi-panique, mais un an plus tard, ils la saluaient comme celle qui avait sauvé l'image de la ville. La comparaison s'arrête là. Miami Vice était tourné dans les rues de Miami et pay

articles.t: Aspects of GTA 6 are inspired by Red Dead Redemption 2
articles.chapeau: "As the resolution goes up, you want the sophistication of the experience to go up."
articles.txt:
(Image credit: Rockstar) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Grand Theft Auto 6 doesn't just mark a huge, and at times unbelievable, step forward for graphics; it's also at the forefront of what an open world game can be, just look at the existential crisis it's given Cyberpunk 2's creative director . With thousands of enterable buildings , unpredictable and slightly scary NPCs , and systems that help you determine what kind of criminal you want to be. It all really does feel like a milestone for what videogames can do.
"As the resolution goes up, you want the sophistication of the experience to go up, and obviously the sophistication of the mechanics," Rob Nelson, Rockstar's head of development, says in an interview with Eurogamer. "So it just naturally flowed that we give players choices to interact with the world beyond just violence, beyond just 'down the barrel of a gun', because it's fun."
The sophisticated mechanics that Nelson is talking about here pertains to GTA 6's Criminal Profile , a system that evaluates your escapades across Leonida and gives you a rating. There's Professional, Hardened, Violent, Psycho, and Irredeemable. The more stealthy and non-lethal you are, the higher your profile will be. It's similar to Red Dead Redemption 2's Honor System .
"There was maybe more emotional resonance in the story of RDR2 than we had, certainly in a GTA before," Nelson says. "So we liked that idea. We didn't necessarily come to GTA 6 going: 'We must have emotional resonance,' but all of those things combine. It's more that those systems and that element of player choice and agency, and the way that affected the narrative, was a hard thing to ignore and walk away from."
Nelson explains that most of the groundwork started as "simple things" in principle, "but they create a lot more work in terms of development of the sophistication of the systems." It's all about choice in GTA 6. You choose whether you want to be a criminal with a conscience or a loose cannon.
"It's still a world of violence, but you could threaten somebody by aiming a gun at them and just robbing them, and they have a chance to comply. So you don't have to beat them to death to get their money."
The part that sticks out the most is that you "don't have to" approach crimes in a certain way, there's still the option to go into every encounter guns blazing because redemption only works from a storytelling perspective when it's the player's choice, and not as Nelson puts it, something that is "foisted upon you".
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.
"You can still go on those rampages and basically smash your Criminal Profile until it breaks," Nelson adds. "And then you enter this irredeemable state, which basically says, 'I reject your criminal profile system! I don't want it.'"
Am I brave enough to reject the criminal profile system entirely? Hell no. I replay sections of dialogue if I accidentally upset someone, and cannot do an "evil run" of a game without giving myself stomach ulcers because of the guilt — but I appreciate having the option.

articles.t: En Normandie, un homonyme du héros de GTA VI écrit à Rockstar Games pour obtenir « un geste ou un message »
articles.chapeau: Homonyme du héros de GTA VI, un Normand a écrit à Rockstar Games pour tenter d’obtenir un clin d’œil dans le jeu vidéo phénomène.
articles.txt:
Homonyme du héros de GTA VI, un Normand a écrit à Rockstar Games pour tenter d’obtenir un clin d’œil dans le jeu vidéo phénomène.
Un Normand a écrit au studio de développement derrière le jeu Grand Theft Auto VI . Rencontré par nos confrères de Paris Normandie , un habitant la ville de Louviers (Eure) a indiqué s’être adressé au studio Rockstar Games pour tenter d’obtenir de leur part « un geste ou un message ».
La raison : il est un homonyme du désormais célèbre Jason Duval , l’un des deux héros de GTA VI. N’ayant pas encore pu mettre la main sur le jeu , ce Normand a découvert la coïncidence lorsque ses collègues de travail la lui ont signalée.
Vidéo GTA 6 : Lucia, l’héroïne qui fait l’effet d’une bombe chez les joueurs
« Au départ, je pensais qu’il n’y avait que le prénom, mais non, c’est bien Jason Duval », a-t-il raconté à nos confrères. Pour l’heure, il n’a obtenu aucune réponse du studio, déjà bien occupé par les tentatives des internautes de pirater leur jeu afin de le rendre disponible sur PC.
Le studio s’est félicité d’un lancement « record » ayant généré 3,8 milliards de dollars de ventes le jour de sa sortie, tandis que Sony a évoqué « le plus grand lancement de l’histoire de la console PlayStation ».

articles.t: Les tronçonneuses « auraient été un peu too much' même pour GTA 6, selon Rockstar qui explique pourquoi certaines armes manquent à l'appel
articles.chapeau: On a vu des joueurs très bien s'en passer...
articles.txt: Vous pouvez commettre des actes de violence extrême dans GTA 6 , grâce à un large éventail d’armes. Armes à feu, battes de baseball, voire des chars d’assaut : tous peuvent devenir vos outils de destruction. Mais cela n’a pas empêché certains de se demander où avaient bien pu disparaître certaines des armes préférées de la série. Parmi celles-ci figurent notamment les katanas et les tronçonneuses, qui étaient des incontournables des jeux de « l’ univers 3D » de Grand Theft Auto, notamment Vice City et San Andreas. La tronçonneuse, en particulier, entretient un lien spécial avec Vice City, compte tenu de ses inspirations évidentes tirées du film Scarface et d’une scène mémorable mettant en scène cet outil dans le film de 1983.

9 games under $15 in Xbox's Black Friday sale if GTA 6 is out of your price range
articles.chapeau: Including savings of up to 90% off 😱
articles.txt:
Xbox's Black Friday sale is underway, and here are nine games you can pick up for less than $15.
It may feel like the entirety of the world is playing Grand Theft Auto VI , and that assertion isn’t far wrong.
If you’re not playing Rockstar Games’ behemoth, though, you’re not alone; GTA VI isn’t everyone’s cup of tea, and for some, it simply isn’t in their price range at £69.99 / $79.99 for the game’s most basic edition.
Thankfully, there’s plenty out there that you can pick up for a steal - especially on Xbox , which has officially launched its Black Friday sale.
We’ve scoured the digital storefront for our best picks; here are nine games you can purchase right now for less than $15.
Save 80 percent on the Tomb Raider: Definitive Survivor Trilogy , which includes three brilliant games for the measly price of $9.99. This is a reboot trilogy, so you don’t need any prior experience with the character; although, let’s be honest, who isn’t familiar with Lara Croft? Tomb Raider serves as an origin story before Lara grows into a fully-fledged hero in Rise of the Tomb Raider and Shadow of the Tomb Raider.
Rise is often considered the trilogy’s best entry, but I’d argue it’s Shadow . While we may have a new Lara in the upcoming 2028 launch Tomb Raider: Catalyst, the game will follow on from this particular trilogy, so there’s no better time to catch up.
First-person shooter Metro Exodus is a steal, with an enormous 90 percent having been wiped off the price for Black Friday. It’s the third instalment in the Metro series, so some familiarity with the franchise is ideal but the plot does function as somewhat of a standalone piece, so you should be fine either way.
Unlike previous entries, Metro Exodus breaks away from a linear formula to introduce some semi-open-world hubs. If you want to shoot your way through a high-octane post-apocalyptic landscape, this 20 to 25 hour experience should keep you satisfied.
Hogwarts Legacy also boasts a 90 percent discount in Xbox’s latest sale, allowing you to sample the Wizarding World RPG ahead of the premiere of HBO’s Harry Potter TV reboot, which actually takes inspiration from the world design of Avalanche Studios’ best-selling title.
The game sees you join Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry in your fifth year, with the playable character able to tap into a powerful ancient magic. With a sequel widely believed to be announced soon, it’s a good time to catch up - and while the open-world is a tad repetitive, exploring Hogwarts itself is a delight.
If you want something a little bit less mainstream, then Cult of the Lamb might be it. Massive Monster and Devolver Digital’s 2022 roguelike remains as brilliant today as it was when it first launched four years ago - and if you like what you play, there are tons of paid DLCs you can add on to extend the base game experience.
It essentially sees you run a cult of, you guessed it, lambs, with the player needing to keep their cult fed, watered, healthy, and warm. That means keeping everyone in line and contributing to your budding society. If they don’t and you’re low on food, they might end up as your next meal.
If GTA VI is a little out of your price range, why not go back and revisit what is arguably the best Grand Theft Auto game out there, prior to GTA VI ’s release. GTA IV is a steal at 65 percent off, with the game following the misadventures of Niko Bellic.
Taking place across Liberty City, Bellic sets out in pursuit of the American Dream like so many others. But he soon becomes enraged in Liberty City’s underworld with the player engages in all kinds of wrongdoing. The density of offerings in Liberty City felt so revolutionary back in 2008, and it’s still a joy to play today.
Final Fantasy VII Revelation is on the way in 2027, so here’s your chance to catch up on the latest instalment, Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, which actually only landed on Xbox earlier this year, having launched on PlayStation back in 2024. With 85 percent off then, that’s a pretty major launch-year discount.
If you love sprawling RPGs, Final Fantasy VII Rebirth is for you. In this particular entry, Cloud Strife and company depart Midgar in pursuit of Sephiroth. With a runtime of 50 to 160 hours, you’re getting plenty of bang for your buck.

articles.t: Why The GTA 6 Team Photo Became A Flashpoint For The Gaming Industry's Diversity Problem
articles.chapeau: A photo apparently showing the people behind GTA VI sparked new debate about Black representation in gaming and who gets hired to build worlds like Vice City.
articles.txt:
Now, a photo showing the people who built it has the internet asking some tough questions and accusing the makers, Rockstar Games, of being racist.
The image, shared by the X account GTA 6 Updates, sparked a debate about Black representation at Rockstar Games and across the gaming industry.
"The people behind GTA 6 🩷" read the caption that went along with the team photos.
It remains unclear who is pictured and how much of the development team the photo represents.
"We really need more black people in tech. GTA shouldn't be this white," one commented on the photo, while another said there is "not a black person in sight is crazy."
Some netizens went further, questioning whether the gaming industry makes room for the people whose culture it draws from.
"Diversity is always an option. They don't mind using parts of our culture for their games though," said one.
One commenter pointed to Rockstar North's location in Scotland and argued that the industry's lack of Black representation stemmed from how few Black people pursued training in game development or design.
"Dude this is Scotland, and if you want the honest truth we aren't in the gaming field. Not because they don't hire us as developers it's not many blacks that went to school for game development/Design. The gaming industry is like 3% black folks."
Others questioned hiring and drew a connection between the culture they see reflected in the games and the people they saw in the photo.
Another wrote, "Tell me you're racist without telling you're racist… lol."
For a crime series that is so steeped in American culture, some might find it surprising that Grand Theft Auto is mostly made in Scotland.
Rockstar Games has a dozen offices around the world, with its power center, Rockstar North, in Edinburgh.
Vice City, the fictional metropolis at the heart of GTA 6, is Rockstar Games' spin on Miami.
To build the fictional city, staff made a series of research trips to Miami, according to Bloomberg.
During the trips, developers tagged along with the city's police officers as they headed to crime hot spots.
They leaned out of helicopters to photograph the city from above and worked their way through packed nightclubs to see how the rooms were lit.
Recreating that atmosphere in Vice City meant animating clubgoers individually, adding drinks and music, and syncing the lights to what was playing.
They intentionally added "layers and layers and layers of detail" to make the virtual club in Vice City look as real and authentic as they possibly could, according to top artist Aaron Garbut.
"And now you understand why it took so long," Jennifer Kolbe, Rockstar's head of publishing, told the outlet last month.
The team has executed research trips even for previous versions of the game. For GTA VI, which came over a decade after the last game, the first research trip happened all the way back in 2015.
Rob Nelson, one of the lead developers on GTA VI, said the team was always "semi-undercover" during these trips.
But he admitted that when there's a "bunch of dorks" making their way through a terrifying neighborhood, they "do stick out a bit."
"Before you're doing hyper-organized research trips, you're immersing yourself in the place and its history, the vibe of it," Nelson told the Guardian earlier this month.
"[You see] the physical places you want to move characters through, the experiences you want them to have, and the juxtaposition between the extremes of society that are in Miami," he added.

La PS5 Pro ajoute des ombres calculées en ray tracing, ce que Rockstar a confirmé, tandis que la Xbox Series S baisserait la qualité des textures et réduirait même la foule dans les rues. Nous avons détaillé cette fuite ici . Rockstar n’a pas commenté le reste de la liste.
Pour un PC, la conséquence est simple : les cartes graphiques de notre guide de configuration visent ces réglages de console. Pour jouer avec une image plus belle que sur PS5, il faudra davantage de puissance.
Pour l’instant, GTA 6 n’existe que sur PS5 et Xbox Series, où il est sorti le 19 novembre. Rockstar n’a annoncé aucune version PC, mais GamesBeat affirme, sur la foi de quatre sources anonymes, qu’elle est prévue pour le premier trimestre 2027 ; le studio n’a pas commenté. Ce serait bien plus rapide que pour GTA 5 , arrivé sur PC en avril 2015, soit environ un an et sept mois après sa sortie sur PS3 et Xbox 360.
L’information la plus solide vient de Digital Foundry , qui a comparé le jeu sur les quatre consoles. Toutes utilisent le ray tracing, une technique qui simule le trajet de la lumière, pour l’éclairage et les reflets. Même la Xbox Series S, la moins puissante , le conserve, quitte à calculer son image en 720p et à passer souvent sous les 30 images par seconde.
Aucune console ne permet de couper le ray tracing. Cela ne dit pas encore ce que proposera la version PC.
C’est un problème pour les PC équipés d’une carte sans circuits dédiés au ray tracing : GeForce GTX (séries 900, 10 et 16), Radeon RX 500 et RX 5000. Elles représentent encore plus de 13 % des PC du sondage Steam d’octobre 2026 . Certaines GTX savent faire du ray tracing grâce à leur pilote, sans circuits dédiés, mais rien ne garantit qu’elles seraient acceptées par GTA 6, ni assez rapides.
La TV Micro RGB 65 » R95H à 1 999€ Black Friday : la TV Samsung Micro RGB 65″ R95H perd 1 000 € et s’affiche à 1 999 € au lieu de 2 999 €, du 21 au 30 novembre. Grâce à sa technologie Micro RGB, il délivre « un niveau de précision et de richesse colorimétrique inédit ».
Trois scénarios sont possibles, sans qu’on sache lequel Rockstar choisira.
Des circuits de ray tracing obligatoires. Ces cartes seraient alors exclues. C’est le choix d’ Indiana Jones et le Cercle ancien et de Doom: The Dark Ages , qui exigent une carte équipée pour le ray tracing.
Un ray tracing logiciel. Comme dans Star Wars Outlaws ou Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora , le jeu calcule alors le ray tracing sans circuits dédiés, et se lance donc sur ces cartes. Dans les tests de TechPowerUp en 1080p, une Radeon RX 5700 XT y fait jeu égal avec une RX 6600, équipée pour le ray tracing, alors qu’elle la devance d’environ 10 % dans les jeux sans ray tracing.
Un mode PC sans ray tracing. Rockstar l’a fait pour GTA 5 Enhanced, la version modernisée de GTA 5 sur PC : le ray tracing y est facultatif, et une GeForce GTX 1630 suffit au minimum.
Si un tel mode existait, le gain pourrait être important. Dans un test de GTA 5 Enhanced réalisé par le site polonais PurePC , activer le ray tracing fait perdre de 41 à 57 % des images par seconde en 1080p sur ces cartes courantes :

articles.t: GTA 6 fait passer la PS5 devant la Switch 2 au Japon
articles.chapeau: Selon Famitsu (16 au 22 novembre 2026), la PS5 devance la Switch 2 au Japon avec 41 472 ventes grâce à GTA 6 (200 759 boîtes) et au modèle Midnight Black.
articles.txt:
La scène était devenue introuvable depuis près d’un an et demi dans les rayons japonais. Selon le relevé hebdomadaire officiel publié par Famitsu pour la semaine du 16 au 22 novembre 2026 , la gamme PlayStation 5 a devancé la Nintendo Switch 2 au Japon. C’est la toute première fois que la console de Sony reprend la tête du classement matériel face à la machine de Kyoto depuis le lancement de cette dernière en juin 2025.
L’écart reste contenu, mais le symbole pèse lourd dans un archipel habituellement verrouillé par Nintendo. Sur les sept jours écoulés, Sony totalise 41 472 PS5 vendues tous modèles confondus, contre 36 817 Nintendo Switch 2 . Une semaine plus tôt, dans le bilan Famitsu du 9 au 15 novembre , la PlayStation 5 plafonnait encore à 11 136 unités derrière les 42 402 Switch 2 écoulées. En sept jours, la console de Sony bondit donc de 272,4 % .
Cette bascule ne doit rien au hasard. Deux sorties majeures ont convergé le jeudi 19 novembre 2026 dans les enseignes nippones. D’abord, Grand Theft Auto VI a pris instantanément la tête du classement software avec 200 759 exemplaires physiques écoulés en quatre jours sur PS5, malgré les ajustements imposés à la version japonaise classée CERO Z .
Il faut toutefois lire ce score avec les précautions d’usage propres à Famitsu. Le cabinet japonais comptabilise les boîtes vendues en magasin (qui renferment un code de téléchargement sur ce lancement), les cartes prépayées et les packs console, mais exclut les achats effectués directement sur le PlayStation Store. Par comparaison, Grand Theft Auto V avait ouvert à 360 115 exemplaires sur PS3 en octobre 2013 au Japon, à une époque où le disque physique représentait encore la quasi-totalité du marché.
Le second moteur, presque tout aussi décisif dans les chiffres matériels, porte un nom précis : la PlayStation 5 Digital Edition Midnight Black réservée au marché japonais (référence CFI-2200B02S). Lancée le même jour par Sony Interactive Entertainment au tarif agressif de 55 000 yens TTC , cette version verrouillée en langue japonaise et sur un compte PSN nippon a absorbé la quasi-totalité de la demande. À elle seule, la PS5 Digital Edition représente 40 362 consoles vendues , soit 97,3 % du volume total de Sony sur la semaine et 3 545 unités de plus que la Switch 2.
Le détail publié par Famitsu met en lumière l’effet spectaculaire de cette édition dédiée au Japon, tandis que la PS5 Standard tombe sous la barre des cent unités hebdomadaires. Même en cumulant la Switch 2 et l’ensemble de la gamme Switch de première génération (41 179 consoles au total), Sony garde une courte avance de 293 machines sur l’ensemble de la semaine.
Par famille de constructeurs, le relevé hebdomadaire s’établit ainsi : 41 472 unités pour la gamme PS5 (cumul de 7 868 730 machines), 36 817 unités pour la Switch 2, 4 362 unités pour la famille Switch première du nom et 751 unités pour la gamme Xbox Series X|S. La PlayStation 5 capte ainsi 49,7 % des 83 402 consoles écoulées dans le pays durant cette semaine événement.
Voir les disponibilités PlayStation 5 Digital Edition sur Amazon →
Si Grand Theft Auto VI écrase les débats en tête avec près de six fois le volume de son dauphin, le reste du classement physique rappelle à quel point le territoire appartient encore à Nintendo. Les neuf autres marches du Top 10 sont intégralement occupées par des jeux Switch 2 et Switch. The Legend of Zelda : Ocarina of Time cède sa première place mais franchit les 658 000 cartouches vendues, tandis que les deux versions de Momotaro Dentetsu 2 reviennent dans le top après la mise en ligne d’une démo Switch 2 le 17 novembre.
Il ne faut pas surinterpréter cette semaine en y voyant un renversement durable du marché japonais. Dès la semaine prochaine, avec les fêtes de fin d’année et l’inertie colossale du catalogue Nintendo, la Switch 2 a toutes les chances de reprendre sa place de numéro un, d’autant que son cumul frôle déjà les 6,7 millions de consoles en moins d’un an et demi.
En revanche, Sony vient de prouver quelque chose d’essentiel sous l’impulsion de Hideaki Nishino : la PS5 n’est pas morte au Japon, elle était simplement devenue trop chère pour le foyer moyen. En alignant un modèle japonais à 55 000 yens exactement le jour où un mastodonte comme GTA 6 arrive en rayon, PlayStation a retrouvé la formule du jeu qui fait vendre une console. Reste à savoir si Sony saura enchaîner d’autres gros rendez-vous exclusifs ou tiers majeurs en 2027 pour éviter que ce sursaut ne res

articles.t: GTA 6 : pourquoi vous ne pouvez pas rejouer les missions
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 ne nous permet pas de rejouer les missions alors que cela était possible dans GTA 5 et Red Dead Redemption 2. En privilégiant cette approche, Rockstar cherche à préserver l'impact de l'histoire et les conséquences de nos décisions.
articles.txt:
GTA 6 ne nous permet pas de rejouer les missions alors que cela était possible dans GTA 5 et Red Dead Redemption 2. En privilégiant cette approche, Rockstar cherche à préserver l’impact de l’histoire et les conséquences de nos décisions.
Si vous avez débuté l’aventure GTA 6 , vous avez probablement remarqué qu’il n’était pas possible de recommencer les missions de l’histoire principale. C’est un changement notable par rapport aux précédents jeux du studio. Dans GTA 5 comme dans Red Dead Redemption 2 , les joueurs pouvaient relancer librement les missions déjà terminées. Pourquoi Rockstar a-t-il décidé de se passer de cette fonctionnalité dans GTA 6 ?
Questionné à ce sujet par le média spécialisé Kotaku, Scott Butchard, directeur de la conception, explique que la rejouabilité des missions était une option “envisagée dès le début du développement” . Décision a finalement été prise de faire une croix dessus. “À mesure que le jeu prenait forme, cette fonctionnalité nous a semblé en contradiction avec l’histoire que nous voulions raconter et paraissait artificielle et déconnectée” , souligne le Senior Design Director.
D’après lui, “sortir de l’intrigue principale pour rejouer des missions aurait diminué sensiblement l’impact des choix faits en jeu” . Pour GTA 6 , le studio a privilégié une narration immersive et évolutive. Au fil de votre progression et de vos choix, les relations entre les personnages changent, les décors se renouvellent et de nouveaux enjeux viennent rythmer l’aventure.
Une mission peut notamment être “le catalyseur qui fera passer d’une partie du jeu à une autre” , pointait ainsi Rob Nelson, codirecteur de Rockstar North . Pouvoir recommencer une mission viendrait ainsi briser cette continuité narrative et fragiliser l’immersion recherchée par le studio.
Il est donc préférable d’effectuer une sauvegarde avant chaque quête importante, afin de pouvoir éventuellement la relancer ultérieurement. S’il est peu probable que Rockstar finisse par autoriser la rejouablité des missions, une telle fonctionnalité devrait être développée par des moddeurs lorsque la version PC sera sortie.

articles.t: GTA 6 Cast: Who Plays Jason and Lucia, and Who Else Is In It
articles.chapeau: Who plays Lucia and Jason in GTA 6: Manni L. Perez and Dylan Rourke, per Rockstar
articles.txt:
Who plays Lucia and Jason in GTA 6: Manni L. Perez and Dylan Rourke, per Rockstar's credits. The main cast, the music cameos and the Florida Joker.
In GTA VI, Jason Duval is played by Dylan Rourke and Lucia Caminos by Manni L. Perez, Rockstar's credits confirm. Neither was confirmed before launch; the two posted together on launch day, 19 November. The main cast also includes Bobby Moynihan, Stephen Root, Roselyn Sanchez, Michael Jai White and Denzel Curry, and the full cast has Kodak Black, Sexyy Red and Big Mike as themselves, Bad Bunny as Mitico Mario and the NFL receiver Tyreek Hill as Maleek Rivers.
For two years the most searched faces in gaming had no names. Rockstar kept the leads secret right up to release, and the internet filled the gap with guesses. Then the credits went live, and most of the guesses turned out to be right.
Rockstar's credits page lists them at the top of the main cast: "Jason Duval: Dylan Rourke" and "Lucia Caminos: Manni L. Perez". On launch day the two put up a joint Instagram post, quoted by Complex: "We are truly honored to collaborate on this worldwide testament to human creativity, ingenuity, and sheer willpower." And: "Keep fighting for what you love. Stay humble. See y'all in Leonida."
The names were not new. They had been going round since 2024, from a YouTuber citing an unnamed source, and two famous voice actors, Troy Baker and Roger Craig Smith, said publicly that they were not Jason. Notebookcheck traced the first firm hints to the days before launch: a Game Awards nomination listing linked Perez to Lucia on 17 November, and IGN's Dutch review named Rourke the next day.
Rockstar has talked about the characters more than the actors. "We wanted them to be people we could like, care about, and root for," Rupert Humphries, its senior VP of narrative, told Game Informer. The actors themselves have not given an interview yet.
Rockstar went to the source rather than to whoever was trending.
The full cast is where it gets fun, and where the music is. Rockstar credits Kodak Black as "Himself", and Complex says he hosts a radio show in the game. Sexyy Red is "Herself". Bad Bunny plays a character called Mitico Mario, on top of hosting Cocoteo FM. Freddie Gibbs plays Freddie. Scott Storch, the producer behind a stack of 2000s hits, plays a character called The Pianist. DJ Stevie J plays Stevie J.
Sport got a slot too. Tyreek Hill plays Maleek Rivers. And one old face is back: Danny Tamberelli plays Jimmy De Santa, the son from GTA V.
On the radio, the credits confirm what was reported in October: Trina and Trick Daddy host Dirty South Classics as themselves, and Gucci Mane is himself on a show called The Tap In. Our guide to all 24 stations has the rest of the hosts, from Palms Trax to PinkPantheress.
From a DJ's chair, the casting tells you where the game's ears are. Kodak Black is from Pompano Beach, Trina and Trick Daddy are Miami, and Rockstar went to the source rather than to whoever was trending. That is why the city sounds right. More on that in our Miami music story .
The most famous "real" face never got a confirmed role. In December 2023 Lawrence Sullivan, the Florida man known online as the Florida Joker, said a Joker-like character in the first trailer was based on him. "Ya'll took my likeness, you took my life," he said, as VGC reported, and he claimed Rockstar owed him up to $2 million. He later dropped the threat, GamesRadar and GameSpot reported.
A Lawrence Sullivan is now listed in the credits, in "The Local Population", a list of about 1,100 names with no characters attached. He says it is him. Rockstar has not said who it is, and nothing in the credits makes him a voice actor. So: a Lawrence Sullivan is credited, and the Florida Joker says it is him. That is as far as the record goes.
For what else is going on with the game, read our launch report , with the scores and the sales so far.

articles.t: GTA 6 Brooks Boatworks walkthrough
articles.chapeau: Here's our complete Brooks Boatworks walkthrough for GTA 6, including all Key Valuable locations.
articles.txt:
Brooks Boatworks in GTA 6 is an Illegal Operation you can raid in Port Gellhorn after completing the ' Slam Dunk ' main story mission. There are Key Valuables in here to collect, as well as extra loot you can grab to boost your overall payout.
On that note, here's my complete Brooks Boatworks walkthrough including all Key Valuable locations .
For more help with your time as Lucia and Jason in Leonida, take a look at our GTA 6 walkthrough .
Brooks Boatworks is in north-west Port Gellhorn , north of the Pay 'n' Spray and north-east of Gellhorn Outfitters. You can find the location marked on the map below:
When you approach the area, be careful as there are Kolts guarding the main entrance and there are a lot of them inside just waiting for you to try something. However, there are ways to get inside without being seen...
I recommend using the gap in the fence by some upturned boats to get into Brooks Boatworks. You can find the location marked on the map below. This particular route will also allow you to sneak past the guards at the entrance. You can also approach by water, but I preferred this method.
There are a total of four Key Valuables in Brooks Boatworks to find and collect. These are alongside other valuables you can grab to fence, such as Cash and Drugs (remember to drop the latter to Dunk's trailer for an early-game cash boost).
The first safe requires a code, and I highly recommend looking for the code because it contains two more important safe codes beside it for other locations. To find the safe code, head into the building on the right side of the Boatworks. I've marked the building on the map below:
In here, look for a map on the wall with several different codes on it. Inspect the map when prompted to learn the code which is 6823 . Now you know this, you can head off to find the safe.
The first safe (which requires the code) is in the main building of the Boatworks but this is well-guarded. I chose to sneak in through the opening by the water and do silent takedowns as I made my way around. Remember, you can use Focus mode to highlight enemies here.
The safe itself is in the office on the first floor of this building.
Now, you can open the safe with force or with Sticky Bombs - but this will draw attention to you, so it's best to use the code.
In this room you can also find two bags of pills and a pack of cigarettes on the pool table, and some cash in a counting machine on the coffee table.
In this room there's a first-aid kit on the wall that contains some Zombix and Adrenaline. Also, on the table near the first-aid kit is an extra dose of Zombix.
The Clunker 556 Assault Rifle can be found on a table inside the building to the right of the Boatworks - the same one where you just found the safe codes (so you may have already picked this up!). I recommend getting this now if you've not grabbed it already, because this weapon makes short work of the Kolts if things get heated.
There's also some cash laying around on the table nearby, grab this to bump up your payout.
There's a first-aid kit on the wall opposite the Assault Rifle, this contains Adrenaline.
Thankfully, the second safe doesn't need a code and can be opened by force. This safe can be found in the back room of the office in the building on the left side of the Boatworks. Again, this is quite heavily guarded, so try to stay stealthy if possible.
When you find the safe, interact with it to force it open and loot the cash inside. However, before you move on, there's also some cash to grab from the counting machine to the right of the safe.
Head to the kitchen area near the safe and you'll find a first-aid kit on the wall that contains Adrenaline. There's also some more cash on the table in here too.
The final Key Valuable is the orange Vapid Smuggler Carara Standout Vehicle - and it's best to leave this until last so you can use it as your getaway vehicle!
The Vapid Smuggler Caracara is parked just outside the building on the left side of the Boatworks. Use Focus mode to highlight it - it'll appear yellow during this. If you're yet to alert the Kolts to your presence, then they're going to notice you now - but it's too late, you're done!
The Caracara is already unlocked and doesn't have an alarm, so you can simply hop into it and speed away. This vehicle sells for $6,325 and costs around $5,550 to register as your own . At this point, it’s well known that Switch 2 is by far the market leader in Japan.
While the PS5 still commands some marketshare, it gets dominated by the Nintendo machine on a weekly basis.
GTA 6’s launch is significant, then, because for the first time in a while it’s pushed Sony’s console in front of the Switch 2 – albeit only by a few thousand units.
According to Famitsu’s latest report, the PS5 sold 41,472 units through the week ending 22nd November, while the Switch 2 managed 36,817 units.
This is an incredibly rare scenario, and likely won’t be repeated again (if ever). But it shows that with the right software, Sony can put up a fight domestically against Nintendo.
The company’s been taking the region a lot more seriously under Japanese CEO Hideaki Nishino, launching more affordable region locked units to try and stimulate interest.
This week saw the release of the new Midnight Black model , which certainly helped contribute to the sales.
But PS5’s success was primarily motivated by GTA 6, which sold a very respectable 200,759 units at retail for the week.
That’s slightly less than GTA 5’s 304,752 units opening in 2013, although remember digital buying habits have changed dramatically in the last 13 years, and GTA 6’s physical release was not particularly compelling as it doesn’t include a disc.
A good week for Sony in its home region, then – one that’s unlikely to be replicated, but should be taken as a sign it can compete with the right lineup and pricing model.

articles.t: GTA 6 on Xbox One Tested: The Power of the Cloud Delivers - Save for One Big Issue
articles.chapeau: Image quality and latency deliver, but what about performance?
articles.txt:
Over the past week, we've been testing GTA 6 on every platform available - including the streamed version of the game exclusive to Xbox platforms. After all, this is the only way to access GTA 6 on last-gen hardware, using the Xbox Cloud Gaming app on Xbox One. So how does the experience hold up? How is Microsoft running two CPU-heavy Xbox Series S instances of GTA 6 on a single Xbox Series X blade server? And is this a genuinely decent way to play the game without a current-gen console?
Let's start with nuts and bolts of the experience. As with other Xbox Cloud Gaming titles, which are streamed from Microsoft servers rather than your own console, the version of GTA 6 you're getting here is the Xbox Series S version. That means a few things just by the nature of the Series S port itself - slightly ropey performance, quality setting cutbacks across the board and a 720p base image upscaled to 1080p using FSR 4.1. However, you do at least get all of the game's major effects intact, including ray-traced lighting, ray-traced reflections and strand-based hair.
And, as you'd hope from a cloud version of the game, performance is exactly as on the base console - which is to say normally in the 20s to 30s, depending on CPU load. However, frame pacing is significantly worse than the real deal, with quicker 16.7ms frames and slower 50.0ms frames surrounding the expected 33.3ms ones. This may be a latency mitigation technique of some kind, but we've reported it to Microsoft and they're looking into it.
Image quality, on the other hand, isn't significantly degraded by the streaming process, with only minor compression artefacts that were mainly noticeable in high-frequency detail like foliage or chain-link fences. In motion, these are harder to spot. The top-end 1440p stream option seems to get a higher bitrate than that afforded to other games - anything up to 37mbps in our testing - perhaps due to GTA 6's headline status amongst Xbox Cloud Gaming titles. For context, another recent graphics-focused 30fps Series S release in Control: Resonant seemed to get only 15 to 27mbps.
Latency is also exceptional - at least in context. We measured around an extra 9ms of added latency compared to running GTA 6 locally on Series S - 184.5ms vs 175.2ms -which is essentially imperceptible for a game that is running on all consoles with around 160 to 180ms of latency anyway . That makes the pace relatively sedate, even when driving or shooting, but it's something that you can get used to over time, and the cloud version doesn't change the equation here. These numbers come from a console attached via ethernet cable to a high-speed fibre connection with a wired controller; your mileage may vary based on location, internet speed, controller latency, display latency and so on.
The one major mystery is just how the game runs as well as it does on the Series X blade servers Microsoft uses for Xbox Cloud Gaming at all. After all, we've previously discussed how the system uses two virtual Series S machines on a single piece of Series X silicon - a strategy that works fine for games that are largely GPU-limited, as the Series X GPU is more than twice as big as that of the Series S. For GTA 6, which often seems to be CPU-limited, how can two instances of the game not compete for that CPU capacity, given that the Series X's CPU is the essentially same as the Series S, only running with slightly higher clocks?
Sometimes, the simplest answer is the correct one. We understand from our sources that for GTA 6 in particular, Microsoft is just running a single instance of GTA 6 per blade, ensuring that there's no contention for CPU resources. That does raise the question of why they couldn't serve the Xbox Series X version of the game, but perhaps that would ramp up power and bandwidth demands to untenable levels.
For the moment though, GTA 6 is well worth playing if you lack access to current generation hardware - and players on Xbox One do get a viable version of the game via Xbox Cloud Streaming at a relatively affordable price, working out to $12 if you buy the largest 50 hour allotment, or up to 15 hours free per month with a Game Pass Ultimate subscription... plus the cost of GTA 6 itself.
We'd of course recommend playing locally to those on Xbox Series S or X, but there's surprisingly little lost in the remote version, save for the frame delivery problems and the same crackling audio issue that exists on real Series S hardware. If those flaws can be fixed,

articles.t: Union Vote Fails In Landslide At GTA 6 Studio Rockstar Games
articles.chapeau: The GTA 6 studio will not formally recognize union members
articles.txt:
Rockstar Games will not be forced to formally recognize a union at the Grand Theft Auto 6 studio after its developers based in the UK voted overwhelmingly against the initiative. The weeks-long voting process played out as Rockstar launched the open-world hit to over 30 million sales in its first day .
Voting began on November 12 and concluded today on November 26 . Workers at Rockstar Games voted 75 percent against the recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union. The initiate would have formalized collective bargaining efforts around things like overtime, bonuses, layoffs, and AI. Developers in favor of unionizing can still work with the IGWB, but there will be no regular meetings with management to hash out new policies.
The IWGB Game Workers Union pushing the vote released the following statement:
For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society – this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favor of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen.
Whilst we haven’t emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for new kinds of conversation to start happening. People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We heard from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions can lead us.
A recognition agreement would have marked a path towards greater workplace democracy. But it’s one route of many. At Rockstar we have already won, and will continue to win, tangible changes that improve our everyday lives. We’ll keep fighting for a say. For pay transparency, contractual overtime pay, and protections against AI and layoffs.
The power to shape our working lives has always been, and will always be, in our hands.
The vote comes roughly a year after Rockstar fired dozens of developers it accused of gross misconduct and breaking confidentiality rules around the development of GTA 6 . The fired workers accused the studio of union busting, which it has denied, and a legal fight has been ongoing over the last 12 months at a labor tribunal. A final judgement in that case is still pending. As recently as this month, members of both sides of the dispute were testifying on the record for the case.

Why GTA VI’s version of Florida feels so real
articles.chapeau: Virtual city expert Emma Fraser explains what makes Rockstar’s latest open world work.
articles.txt:
Entertainment Gaming Report Why GTA VI’s version of Florida feels so real Virtual city expert Emma Fraser explains what makes Rockstar’s latest open world work.
Andrew Webster Nov 26, 2026, 3:00 PM UTC Link Share Gift Image: Rockstar Games via The Verge Part Of Grand Theft Auto VI has arrived see all updates Andrew Webster is an entertainment editor covering streaming, virtual worlds, and every single Pokémon video game. Andrew joined The Verge in 2012, writing over 4,000 stories. There are plenty of reasons why Grand Theft Auto VI is so popular : the 13 years of anticipation , the relatable lead characters and romantic storyline , the sheer level of depth . But another major factor is the sense of place. The GTA series is unmatched when it comes to re-creating the feeling of a bustling, real-world city, and GTA VI ’s fictional rendition of Florida is the studio’s most lifelike setting yet. It has functioning buses and trains, plentiful buildings you can go into and explore, residents you can chat with, and huge areas where you can interact with wildlife far away from the bright lights of the Miami-like Vice City. For Emma Fraser , an assistant professor at UC Berkeley who studies urban ruins and virtual cities, the sense of realism has created a unique sensation while playing.
“There’s something about this particular game that is really discombobulating and distracting in a sense,” she says. “Because you have these moments where you think, ‘I’m in a place, I’m experiencing a location.’ You comprehend intellectually that it’s not real or that it’s at best a representation, but you still have this feeling in your brain and you’ll still dream about being in that place.”
Fraser teaches courses on topics including urban geography and virtual worlds and has written papers exploring topics like “mapping in the digital age” and “the virtual spectacle of the end of the city.” She says she started researching video game cities in part because, despite their influence and reach, they’re an underexplored space in academia. “I’m a geographer, and geographers are obsessed with cities,” she explains. “So much of geography is thinking about: How do we imagine cities? How do we navigate cities? How do we build cities? How do we map cities? And video games have all of that, but they’re not taken that seriously as an academic interest.”
Like much of the world, she’s been looking forward to GTA VI for years, particularly because of Rockstar’s on-the-ground approach to research. Before development on the game began, developers from the studio traveled to Florida to get an accurate picture. As GTA VI producer Rob Nelson told me , the starting point for the game was the setting, rather than the story or characters. “We just went around to feel it out,” he said. “Go to the Everglades, go to the Keys, go to the city, as many places as we can, and start thinking about what aspects of the place we want to incorporate.”
While there are plenty of open-world games, many of the most successful — from Elden Ring to The Witcher — are sent in fantastical spaces. GTA stands apart in how its various settings look and feel true to the real world. And Fraser believes that this is one of the key reasons the series has such universal appeal. “You know immediately how to function in a city,” she explains. “You know there’s going to be law enforcement, there are going to be city blocks, there are going to be pedestrians, cars, and buses. It’s this really interesting environment that gives you a lot of possibilities to get a player more immersed in your world, because they already know a lot about a city as a general concept.”
Fraser describes GTA VI ’s world as having “implied expansiveness.” It’s not a one-to-one re-creation of the real location. There are plenty of things missing; you don’t see schools or daycares, and parking spaces are relatively sparse. But the game gets enough details right to be recognizable. Fraser explains that as long as certain parts of the city look correct — the lighting, the coastline, the decoration of street corners, the major arterial roads — that’s enough to convince people that they’re in something resembling Miami.
“You can’t hold a whole city in your mind at one time,” she says. “Instead it’s these highlights. What [Rockstar] do very successfully in the game is those snapshots. articles.t: How to unlock GTA 6 hurricanes and fix the weather bug on PS5
articles.chapeau: Rock your game like a hurricane 🌀
articles.txt:
GTA 6 has some wild weather, but a mysterious PS5 bug effectively disables them. Here's how to fix that and add hurricanes to the mix.
GTA 6 introduces one of the most dynamic weather systems we’ve ever seen in a Rockstar game, so it’s too bad so many PlayStation 5 owners are reporting the same bug. Worry not though, we have a fix and a way of making the in-game weather twice as crazy.
In the opening chapters of GTA VI the weather is meant to be tame. It’s often lovely and sunny so you can effectively soak up the tropical vibes as you live the short-lived good life of Chapter 1.
You can expect the in-game weather to kick it up a notch from Chapter 3 onwards, but to unlock hurricanes you’ll have to engage with one of the game’s side-missions.
To start with you’ll need to head North to Lake Leonida. It’s up in Leonard County and you can’t miss it; it’s huge.
Either drive around the lake or grab a boat and travel across it until you reach a trailer park. Just down the road from that trailer park is a large, fenced-off area with a bunker in the middle. You’ll know you’ve found the right place as automated warnings will start blaring from nearby speakers.
Next, you need to head into the complex. I grabbed a bulldozer around the back and used it as a makeshift ramp so I could hop over the electric fence. Then just avoid the landmines hidden on the ground, destroy the drones that head your way and approach the bunker door.
You’ll be greeted by its owner who tells you to leave and come back later, as he’ll have upgraded his defenses by then and is curious to see if you can make it back in.
Leave, do some side-activities and return when he texts you to say he’s ready. When you come back the easiest way in is jumping from the nearby water tower, and when you successfully make your way to the bunker again he’ll let you inside.
White you’re chatting, a hurricane will roll in outside and once you leave this unique weather-type will occur randomly for the rest of your playthrough.
Now, some PS5 owners are saying their copy of GTA VI isn’t cycling through the various options while they play.
If your version of Leonida is perpetually shrouded in sunlight here’s what you need to do – it’s very easy.
According to GameRoll_ on X, you must first close the game and turn off your PS5. Don’t put it into Rest Mode – shut it down completely.
Then press and hold the power button until the console launches in safe mode, and plug in a controller. Clear the system cache and once that’s been done load GTA VI back up.
This apparently makes the in-game weather changes happen more frequently, and while I’m not entirely sure if I was experiencing the same bug or not, when I attempted this myself last night and played for a few hours it did feel like something had changed.
All of this is well-worth doing, especially for the hurricanes. They’re an awesome modifier for the open-world and make everything feel so much more atmospheric and dangerous.

articles.t: GTA 6 Encrypted Hard Drive: What Is on It?
articles.chapeau: What is on the encrypted hard drive in GTA 6? A senator, partial footage and a lot of unconfirmed claims. Here is what reports back up.
articles.txt:
Image: Rockstar Games Spoiler warning: this article discusses a story item and a scene from Grand Theft Auto VI . If you want to find it yourself, stop here.
The encrypted hard drive is a story item in Grand Theft Auto VI , and players have spent days trying to work out what it holds. Beebom’s spoiler piece, which asked what is on the drive and claimed to answer it, became the top gaming story of the week. The honest answer is narrower than the headline suggests. The game decrypts part of the drive and shows footage of a woman referred to as “Senator.” It never shows the whole thing.
That gap between what the game shows and what the internet claims is the real story. Since GTA 6 reached PS5 and Xbox , players have pulled every thread in Leonida, and the encrypted drive is one of the loudest. This analysis separates what reports confirm from what they only suggest, explains why Rockstar might have built the scene this way, and lays out what to watch next.
Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google
Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.
Start with the basics. The encrypted hard drive is a story item inside the game, and reports place it in a bag alongside a statue. That is the full extent of what the fact record says about where it sits. Nothing in the coverage I reviewed gives a mission name, a map location or a sequence number, so this article does not invent one.
Why does a bag with a statue matter? Because it frames the drive as something a character wanted hidden or moved. A drive tucked in with a statue reads as cargo, not as a keepsake. That framing is analysis, not confirmed lore, and it should stay labeled that way. What reports do confirm is the pairing itself and the fact that the drive is encrypted.
Encryption is the key design signal here. A locked drive promises a payoff, and the game follows through by decrypting some of it. Players then see the result on screen, which is why the story spread so fast. The reveal is visual, short on explanation and heavy on implication.
The game shows decrypted video footage involving a woman referred to as “Senator.” Reports agree the footage includes the senator using drugs. That is the confirmed visual content, and it is the only content the reporting supports. Everything else attached to this scene needs a caveat.
The second confirmed point matters just as much. The footage is only a partial decryption. The game does not reveal the full contents of the drive, and reports say so directly. A player who watches the scene and walks away believing they have seen everything has misread it.
Think of it as a trailer for a document. The decrypted slice proves the drive holds compromising material and tells you who the material concerns. It does not tell you why the drive exists, who made it, or who wants it. Those gaps are where the speculation lives.
Several reports identify Camila Fuentes as the senator in the footage. That identification is itself confirmed as a pattern of reporting. Whether Fuentes is truly the woman on screen is a different question, and it stays unconfirmed. The coverage is inconsistent, and no official Rockstar source backs the match.
This distinction trips up a lot of readers. “Several outlets say X” and “X is true” are separate claims. When outlets copy each other, repetition looks like corroboration even though it is one source echoed five times. Treat the Fuentes name as a strong lead from players and writers, not as a character sheet from Rockstar.
The cautious reading holds up well. The game calls the woman “Senator,” which is a title, not a name. A name attached to that title in reporting could come from other scenes, dialogue or in-game documents that outlets stitched together. Without the underlying source, nobody can verify the link from the outside.
The unconfirmed list is longer than the confirmed one, and that is by design. Below is the clean split, built only from the fact record.
One report says the drive contains footage of Fuentes calling an unknown man “daddy” or “papi.” No other verified source repeats it. Treat it as a rumor until someone shows the scene with timestamps, or until Rockstar confirms it. It may be accurate. The point is that nobody has demonstrated it.

articles.txt:
En quelques jours, des fans ont lancé une version pirate de GTA 6 sur PC à partir d’une fuite Xbox, alors que seul le jeu console est sorti. Ce coup de force inédit ouvre un bras de fer explosif avec Rockstar, dont l’issue reste très incertaine.
Grand Theft Auto VI est officiellement sorti le 19 novembre 2026 sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S , sans aucune date PC confirmée. Pourtant, quelques jours ont suffi pour que des développeurs passionnés fassent démarrer une version pirate de GTA 6 sur Windows à partir d’une build Xbox de 209 Go, complétée par un exécutable de 57 Mo publié par le groupe Cyberleek , comme le rappellent Les Numériques. Du jamais vu à cette vitesse.
Autour de projets comme Leonida , VIctory ou XCL , la communauté s’est fixé un objectif résumé par GameStar : avoir « GTA 6 pour PC avant GTA 6 pour PC ». Serveurs Discord géants, centaines de forks sur GitHub, outils d’IA pour aider au portage, tout s’est emballé en quelques heures. Reste à savoir si ce tour de force doit vraiment inquiéter Rockstar Games ou si l’éditeur peut, pour l’instant, dormir tranquille.
La base de tout, c’est la fuite de la version Xbox de GTA 6 , incluant les données complètes et l’exécutable. Les projets non officiels utilisent soit une recompilation statique, comme Leonida, qui traduit le binaire Xbox en binaire Windows, soit une couche de compatibilité comme XCL qui simule l’environnement de la console. Des outils d’IA servent à analyser le code et générer des portions compatibles PC plus vite qu’à la main.
Résultat concret : XCL affiche déjà les menus de GTA 6 à environ 30 images par seconde, en avalant près de 15 Go de RAM. VIctory va plus loin en chargeant le monde ouvert en une cinquantaine de secondes, mais la scène reste quasi noire et tourne à quelques fps seulement. Certains forks rapportent 22 fps pendant une quarantaine de minutes avant un crash de la carte graphique.
Leonida, lui, affirmait avoir converti tous les shaders et promettait une version jouable en « au moins une semaine » avant de disparaître. Malgré cette avancée, on est encore loin d’un jeu réellement praticable : pas de stabilité, pas de GTA Online , accès réservé à une poignée d’utilisateurs capables de manipuler une fuite illégale de plus de 200 Go.
Pour les joueurs PC, ces démonstrations prouvent surtout que GTA 6 tourne déjà, d’une façon ou d’une autre, sur leur plateforme alors que Take Two Interactive n’a toujours pas annoncé de version Windows. Comme pour GTA V et Red Dead Redemption 2 , la stratégie semble rester console d’abord, PC plus tard, des sources de l’industrie évoquant seulement un créneau autour du premier trimestre 2027.
En parallèle, les médias français alertent sur la prolifération de faux « GTA 6 PC » truffés de malwares. Télécharger une version piratée expose à des chevaux de Troie, mais aussi à des risques juridiques bien réels : en France, la contrefaçon d’une œuvre protégée peut entraîner jusqu’à 3 ans de prison et 300 000 € d’amende, même si l’ARCOM est moins visible qu’à l’époque de la Hadopi.
Pour jouer légalement sur un PC aujourd’hui, la seule voie reste le streaming depuis une console via Remote Play ou équivalent Xbox, avec un exemplaire acheté de manière classique. Tout le reste, qu’il s’agisse de builds compilées à partir de la fuite ou de faux installateurs, reste à éviter.
La réaction de Take Two a été immédiate. Le 24 novembre 2026, une plainte DMCA a conduit GitHub à retirer Leonida et 3 007 dépôts associés. Le serveur Discord du projet, qui avait atteint environ 179 000 membres, a été fermé, tout comme le compte du développeur principal, âgé de 15 ans, selon Frandroid. GameStar parle d’un « jeu du chat et de la souris » à une échelle inédite.
Sur le plan commercial, l’impact semble pourtant limité à court terme. Les versions actuelles sont instables, techniquement hors de portée du grand public et totalement privées de composante en ligne. Les quelques milliers de curieux capables de les lancer sont, pour la plupart, le cœur de cible qui achètera aussi la version officielle console ou PC.
Le vrai risque pour Rockstar se situe plutôt du côté de l’image et du contrôle de son jeu phare. Voir circuler des séquences illisibles à 5 fps sous l’étiquette « GTA 6 PC » brouille le message et met en lumière une faille de sécurité majeure. Mais cette agitation entretient aussi une visibilité énorme autour de GTA 6 et confirme l’appétit du public pour un portage Windows. Tant que Rockstar garde la main sur la version définiti

articles.t: GTA 6 : une fuite détaille les écarts graphiques entre PS5, PS5 Pro et Xbox
articles.chapeau: Une fuite des réglages graphiques de GTA 6 détaille plein de petits détails techniques sur les versions du jeu comme les ombres en ray tracing de la PS5 Pro. Sur Xbox Series S, les compromis iraient même jusqu’à réduire le trafic et le nombre de piétons dans Vice City.
articles.txt:
Une fuite des réglages graphiques de GTA 6 détaille plein de petits détails techniques sur les versions du jeu comme les ombres en ray tracing de la PS5 Pro. Sur Xbox Series S, les compromis iraient même jusqu’à réduire le trafic et le nombre de piétons dans Vice City.
Si toutes les versions de GTA 6 tournent à 30 images par seconde, la qualité des graphismes varie d'une console à l'autre. ©RichieSanders x Shutterstock Les différences entre les versions console de GTA 6 se verraient jusque dans les embouteillages de Vice City. Rockstar vise 30 images par seconde sur les quatre machines, et un relevé de réglages que le dataminer Tex2 dit avoir tiré des fichiers du jeu donne un aperçu des compromis faits pour tenir cette cadence.
Partagé le 25 novembre sur X par Tex2, le document a depuis disparu du réseau social. Heureusement, certains sites comme MP1st, ont pu reproduire les tableaux des réglages graphiques de GTA 6 , console par console.
Dans ces tableaux, la PS5 standard et la Xbox Series X partagent les mêmes réglages graphiques. Les textures et la tessellation, qui subdivise les surfaces pour affiner leur géométrie, y sont réglées sur « élevé ». L’illumination globale, le calcul des rebonds de la lumière entre les surfaces, reste sur « moyen ». Rockstar avait déjà précisé que les deux consoles calculent leur image en 1440p avant de la reconstruire en 4K avec le même algorithme maison d’anticrénelage temporel, ou TAA.
La PS5 Pro conserve les textures en qualité élevée et part elle aussi du 1440p. Elle s’appuie sur le PSSR 2 de Sony pour reconstruire l’image en 4K. Rockstar avait déjà confirmé qu’elle serait la seule à calculer des ombres en ray tracing .
D’après le relevé, l’illumination globale passerait sur « élevé ». Le lancer de rayons servirait à calculer l’ombre d’un arbre au soleil aussi bien que celle d’un passant sous un lampadaire. Les réglages correspondants, pour les ombres directionnelles et les ombres liées aux sources de lumière locales, seraient tous deux sur « élevé ». Leurs équivalents calculés par rastérisation passeraient sur « faible ».
Sur Series S, Rockstar part d’une image en 720p que le FSR 4 d’AMD reconstruit en 1080p. Les développeurs disent avoir tenu à conserver l’illumination globale en ray tracing malgré la mémoire plus limitée de la console. D’après les tableaux, la qualité des textures et celle de la simulation de l’eau et des vagues reculeraient à « moyen ». La tessellation, elle, tomberait sur « faible ».
L’écart se verrait aussi dans la rue. Sur Series S, la densité des piétons et celle du trafic seraient toutes deux réglées sur « moyen », contre « élevé » sur les trois autres consoles. Le même écart apparaît dans les réglages de la physique et dans plusieurs paramètres de l’IA. Comme quoi, même à Vice City, le diable se cache dans les détails.
GTA VI 79,99 € Foire aux questions Contenu généré par l’IA Quelle est la différence entre la rastérisation et le ray tracing pour calculer les ombres dans un jeu ? La rastérisation calcule l’image en projetant des triangles sur l’écran, puis en appliquant des astuces (shadow maps, filtrage, biais) pour simuler les ombres à moindre coût. Le ray tracing, lui, lance des rayons dans la scène pour déterminer si un point est éclairé ou occulté, ce qui produit des ombres généralement plus cohérentes (contacts plus crédibles, pénombres mieux gérées). En pratique, le ray tracing est nettement plus gourmand en calcul et en bande passante mémoire, d’où des choix ciblés (activer certaines ombres RT et baisser d’autres réglages). Beaucoup de jeux combinent les deux : RT pour quelques effets « premium », rastérisation pour le reste afin de tenir une cadence stable.
L’upscaling reconstruit une image de sortie (1080p/4K) à partir d’un rendu interne plus bas (720p/1440p) pour réduire la charge GPU tout en gardant une image détaillée. Le TAA (Temporal Anti-Aliasing) exploite plusieurs images successives et les vecteurs de mouvement pour lisser les bords et stabiliser le rendu, mais il peut introduire du flou ou des artefacts sur les fins détails. PSSR 2 (Sony) et FSR 4 (AMD) sont des techniques de reconstruction qui utilisent elles aussi des informations temporelles et spatiales, avec des approches et une qualité variables selon le contenu affiché. Le principe reste le même : économiser du calcul en rendu natif, puis « remonter » la définition pour viser une sortie 4K ou 1080p plus propre.

articles.t: GTA 6 recomp hits 90% progress – and here's what that means
articles.chapeau: Less than three days after the previously missing executable file from the leaked Xbox build of GTA 6 was released, the unofficial PC version is already approaching the 30 FPS mark. According to a community tracker, development progress has surpassed 90%. But what exactly does that mean?
articles.txt:
As we previously reported, many PC gamers are frustrated by the lack of an official PC version of GTA 6 . Some have already stated that they intend to play an unofficial recompilation once it's ready – and that could happen sooner rather than later. The community-run website PortWatchVI , which tracks the development of unofficial PC ports, now monitors 39 different projects. According to the website's scoring system, the leading project, known as CGBJ, has already reached 91.5% completion.
The percentages displayed on PortWatchVI are based on a proprietary scoring system that weighs five factors:
The 91.5% figure is not an average across all projects but refers specifically to the current frontrunner, CGBJ. According to PortWatchVI, the project now achieves an average of 25 FPS during gameplay and 30 FPS in cutscenes. Visual quality is reportedly largely on par with the console version, aside from minor rendering issues, while crashes are said to be infrequent. According to the developer, 80% of the story is already playable. Progress is currently being made at a remarkable pace. During our research alone, the completion rating displayed on PortWatchVI climbed from 89.8% to 91.5%.
ⓘ Marius Mülller for Notebookcheck PC performance figures for CGBJ's GTA 6 recompilation, as tracked by PortWatchVI. (Screenshot from PortWatchVI.) Community is thinking in days rather than months The rapid progress is fueling growing excitement within the community. Some users are hoping to play GTA 6 ( currently available on Amazon for $80 ) on PC as early as this coming weekend. While that cannot be ruled out, there is still considerable room for optimization. According to comments on a since-deleted gameplay video of the CGBJ project posted on Reddit , GPU utilization was as low as 5%, while the CPU was under heavy load. This suggests that performance may currently be limited primarily by a CPU bottleneck, leaving considerable scope for improvements through further optimization. For now, however, that remains speculation. In any case, it will be interesting to see how the recompilation projects progress over the coming days.

Sur console, GTA 6 n’affiche aucun menu graphique : le jeu de Rockstar, sorti le 19 novembre sur PS5 et Xbox Series, tourne à 30 images par seconde partout, sans dire ce que chaque machine sacrifie.
Un dataminer surnommé Tex2, qui fouille les fichiers du jeu, a trouvé la liste de ces réglages console par console. Son message sur le forum GTAForums a été supprimé depuis, mais le site MP1st l’a recopié ce mercredi 25 novembre .
